about: A landmark intent (docs/design/world-squares.md section 2; Chem.LandmarkIntent): what a world square asks for, never where it goes. Each form under "by" is how it comes out in a biome (an id in world/biomes.json; "use" borrows another form, "*" is any biome not named). LandmarkIntent.Make turns (intent, biome, site, seed) into rows the map files already read: stamps.json stamps, a villages.json village, buildings.json rows, things.json things per chunk and a places.json place. Offsets are cells from the site, y grows south; the seed turns the whole form a quarter turn or not, and picks the names, the village's seed and every spread. A village is laid one of three ways: "square" (the default), a villages.json recipe laid by VillageLayout; "climb", houses either side of a way climbing from its foot towards the landmark, ending at a "top" house; "wind", a way winding "span" degrees round the landmark from its foot, closing in to "to" cells inside its first stamp's radius (a gentle grade, never its top), with houses on its up slope and its down slope by turns; "shore", houses on an arc "span" degrees round the lake "around", facing the water, with a way between them and the shore. A climb's or a shore's houses are buildings.json rows of the village style, stone by "stoneInTen", with a place of their own. A range [a, b] is a seeded pick, both ends included. Land is in land units (0.125 m). A stamp's "bare" is the terrain it leaves where it moves the land, its trees gone (a volcano's rock). A great tree is a log trunk "trunk" cells across, drawn "flare" metres high under the view's own tree of kind "tree" (a broad one) "scale" times its size (the great-tree detail), with "roots" of fallen tree "root" cells long. Things keep off every row.

temperate.name: a forest village by a great tree

mountains.name: a village at a volcano's foot

foggy-marsh.name: a fishing village on the lake
